transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What has been bothering you or bringing you in?

I feel like I’m constantly worrying about money and my future, from the moment I wake up until I go to bed, and it’s taking over everything. It just feels like I can't catch my breath or find any peace anymore.
Did these worries begin after a specific stressful event or major life change, or have they been going on more generally without one clear trigger? About how long has this been happening?

This constant, all-day worry has been my baseline for a little over a year now. It first started escalating after my divorce settlement two years ago left me with tighter finances, but it really took off about a year ago when I started planning a preschool venture and looking hard at my financial future.

When your worry is at its worst, does it still feel tied mainly to the divorce and financial stress, or has it spread into lots of other areas even when nothing new is happening? Has it continued even during times when those stressors were less intense?

It has definitely spread to almost everything, and it feels like a constant low-grade alarm going off in my head all day. Even minor things, like buying new crayons for my classroom, now trigger intense anxiety about whether I’m going to end up bankrupt in ten years. It just doesn't let up, even when the bigger stressors are relatively quiet.

Along with the constant worry, have you also been having symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, trouble concentrating, muscle tension, irritability, or problems sleeping? If so, which ones have been happening most days?

Yes, I’ve been struggling with several of those almost daily. I lie awake for hours running numbers in my head, only to wake up at three in the morning unable to get back to sleep. On top of that, my mind constantly blanks during staff meetings or when I'm writing lesson plans, and my shoulders and neck feel like I'm carrying a heavy backpack of rocks because I'm clenching my jaw so tight.

How much is this anxiety interfering with your daily life, like your work, relationships, or taking care of things at home? Have you started avoiding situations or making changes because of the worry?

It’s interfering a great deal; I’ve started turning down leadership opportunities at school and stalling on my preschool venture because my head is just too cluttered to make decisions. At home, I even let bills and basic chores pile up because I’m so tied in knots with worry that I just can't bring myself to deal with them.

Do you ever get sudden surges of intense fear or physical symptoms that peak within minutes, like your heart racing, shaking, sweating, shortness of breath, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen? Or is the anxiety more of a steady, ongoing worry throughout the day?

It is definitely more of a steady, ongoing worry throughout the day rather than sudden spikes of panic. It feels like a low-grade alarm is constantly running in the background from the moment I wake up until I go to bed. I don't really experience those sudden physical surges or panic attacks, just this non-stop worrying.

Have you been using any substances or medicines that can make anxiety worse, like a lot of caffeine, stimulants, decongestants, cannabis, or thyroid medication? And do you have any medical problems such as thyroid issues that started around the same time as the anxiety?

No, I don't use any of those substances or medications, and I don't drink excessive caffeine or use cannabis. I also don't have any medical issues, like thyroid problems, that started around the same time as my anxiety.
Along with the anxiety, have you been feeling depressed most days or lost interest in things you usually enjoy? If yes, has that lasted at least two weeks in a row?

I wouldn't say I feel deeply depressed, but I have definitely lost interest and pleasure in the things I used to enjoy. For example, I find myself sitting in my garden unable to enjoy the plants I've tended, or repeatedly checking my bank account instead of practicing my guitar. This has been going on for much longer than two weeks—it has really been my baseline for over a year now.

During this past year, have you also felt down, sad, or hopeless most days for at least two weeks at a time, or is it mainly anxiety and loss of enjoyment without feeling depressed? Did those low-mood feelings begin only after the divorce and financial stress, or do they persist even when those stressors are quieter?

It is definitely more about the constant anxiety and losing touch with my hobbies, rather than feeling down, sad, or hopeless in a depressed way. My mind is just constantly racing with financial calculations, and I feel completely consumed, distracted, and exhausted by the non-stop worry about my future.

Even if you don’t feel deeply depressed, have you been feeling persistently low or blue on most days for at least several weeks along with the anxiety? Or is your mood generally okay aside from being tense, worried, and unable to enjoy things?

No, I don't feel persistently low or blue. My mood is really just dominated by being extremely tense, worried, and unable to enjoy anything. I've completely stopped enjoying my usual hobbies, like tending my garden or practicing the guitar, because my mind is constantly hijacked by financial worries.

This is accompanied by insomnia, impaired concentration, muscle tension, and significant functional impairment at work and home. Although anhedonia is present, the patient denied persistent depressed mood, making generalized anxiety disorder the best fit.
